script: Is Kawhi Leonard the costliest free agency signing of all time? Back in 2019, Kawhi Leonard was the biggest name in free agency, fresh off a championship, and he agreed to sign with the Clippers on one condition. They had to go get his friend Paul George too, so the Clippers made the trade and sent Oklahoma City a young guard named Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, Danilo Gallinari, five first-round picks, and two pick swaps. But the throw-in guard nobody talked about is the reason that trade still haunts them today. Shai became an MVP, while Kawhi kept getting hurt year after year, and the Clippers only reached the conference finals one time in seven seasons. The trade already looked bad, and then on September 2nd, 2026, it got so much worse. But the trade itself was never the part that made this the costliest signing in history. The NBA found the Clippers were secretly paying Kawhi extra money through no-show endorsement deals to get around the salary cap, including one worth $28 million. So the league dropped the hammer. They suspended owner Steve Ballmer for a full year, fined the team $30 million, and took away five more first-round picks from 2029 through 23. The last time a team got caught doing this, the fine was only $3.5 million. So, yes, when you add up an MVP, roughly ten first-round picks, and thirty million dollars, Kawhi Leonard is the costliest signing basketball has ever seen.
